subject: Release train notes (Feb 24): Auto-rollback on SLO breach — feature flag defaults + staged enablement + backout

body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 4:12 PM PST
Subject: Release train notes (Feb 24): Auto-rollback on SLO breach — feature flag defaults + staged enablement + backout

Hi Marissa / Sean,

Putting together release train notes for next week (Feb 24 train) and want to confirm the final posture for the auto-rollback on SLO breach integration.

Please confirm / correct the below so we can publish it to the train channel + the release doc:

1) Feature flags + defaults
- rollout.slo_eval.enabled
  - dev/staging: ON
  - prod: ON (evaluation only) OR OFF? (need decision)
- rollout.auto_action.enabled (executor: pause/rollback)
  - dev/staging: ON
  - prod: OFF by default
- rollout.auto_action.mode
  - staging: rollback_allowed
  - prod: pause_only for first week? (or rollback_allowed but gated by allowlist)

2) Staged enablement proposal
- Staging: enable for internal canary route(s) immediately after deployment
- Prod: enable evaluation (no action) for 24h, then enable pause_only for 1 internal route, then allowlist expansion
- Region order: us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1

3) Backout
- Single switch: rollout.auto_action.enabled=OFF globally
- If evaluator is causing controller load, also flip rollout.slo_eval.enabled=OFF
- Roll back controller build only if flags don’t stabilize

If you can reply with the final answers (esp. prod defaults + first prod canary), I’ll lock the train notes and attach the checklist.

Thanks,
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: AutoRollback_ReleaseTrain_Checklist_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 5:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train notes (Feb 24): Auto-rollback on SLO breach — feature flag defaults + staged enablement + backout

Connor — a few SRE notes.

Prod defaults:
- Please do NOT enable actions globally out of the gate.
- I’m OK with evaluator ON in prod (it’s useful signal), but we need “fail open” behavior when monitors are missing/stale, and we should treat missing monitor as a “no action + emit event” path.

Suggested staged enablement:
- Day 0 (deploy): evaluator ON, executor OFF. Verify dashboards + event stream volume.
- Day 1: enable pause_only for a single internal route in us-west-2 (no rollback yet).
- Day 2-3: expand to us-east-1 + eu-west-1 for same route, still pause_only.
- After a week with low false positives: allow rollback_allowed, still behind allowlist.

Backout:
- Agree: executor OFF is the primary backout.
- Secondary: evaluator OFF if we see telemetry lag or controller hot loops.

Also please call out: alerts should be notify-only initially (no paging), except “rollback executor failure” which should page the owning oncall once rollback is enabled.

-Sean

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 5:27 PM PST
Subject: Re: Release train notes (Feb 24): Auto-rollback on SLO breach — feature flag defaults + staged enablement + backout

+1 to Sean’s plan.

From Product side, please make sure the notes reflect:
- MVP is “pause” first. Rollback is permitted only after we have confidence in monitor coverage + policy bounds.
- Console will show auto actions + suppressions even in evaluator-only mode (so customers/internal users can see the audit trail without us taking action).

For the “single internal route” canary, I suggest the Hosted API chat route for internal org only (we can keep scope tight with customer tier = internal).

Marissa

---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 8:14 AM PST
Subject: Re: Release train notes (Feb 24): Auto-rollback on SLO breach — feature flag defaults + staged enablement + backout

Thanks — I’ll update the train notes accordingly.

Proposed final wording (please sanity check):

Feature flags (prod defaults)
- rollout.slo_eval.enabled = ON
  - Evaluates burn-rate windows for configured rollout scopes.
  - Missing/stale monitor => no action (emit “monitor_missing_or_stale” event).
- rollout.auto_action.enabled = OFF
  - Executor disabled by default; no automatic pause/rollback.
- rollout.auto_action.mode = pause_only (effective once auto_action.enabled is turned on for allowlisted scopes)

Staged enablement schedule
- Feb 24 (deploy): prod evaluator-only, executor OFF
- Feb 25: enable executor for internal allowlist only, us-west-2 only, pause_only
- Feb 26-27: expand same allowlist to us-east-1, then eu-west-1 (pause_only)
- Mar 2+: consider rollback_allowed behind allowlist (requires SRE signoff + game-day outcome review)

Backout instructions
- Immediate: set rollout.auto_action.enabled=OFF (global) to stop all auto actions
- If controller load/telemetry issues: also set rollout.slo_eval.enabled=OFF
- If still unstable: roll back to previous controller release + disable new alert rules (notify-only) as needed

I’ll also add “notify-only alerts” note with the one exception (executor failure pages once rollback is allowed).

Attachment is the enablement snippet I’m putting into the release doc.

Connor

Attachment: staged-enablement-plan-auto-rollback_2026-02-20.txt (text/plain)

Looks good.

Two minor edits:
1) Add explicit guardrail language: “minimum sample size gating + debounce/holdoff means we shouldn’t oscillate; if we do, treat as bug and keep executor OFF.”
2) For Feb 25 enablement, note we need the dashboard + monitor coverage check to be green (the release gate) before flipping executor ON.

Otherwise approved from SRE.

-Sean
